glossary.proximal muscle: Muscles close to the trunk, such as around the shoulders and hips.
glossary.carotid arteries: The main arteries in the neck supplying the head and brain.
glossary.bilateral: Affecting both sides of the body.
glossary.active movement: Movement the patient makes by themselves, limited in PMR by pain.
glossary.low-grade fever: A mildly raised temperature, usually 37.5 to 38.3°C.
glossary.anorexia: Loss of appetite (not the eating disorder).
glossary.formal power testing: Examining muscle strength against resistance, graded 0 to 5.
glossary.inflammatory markers: Blood tests that rise with inflammation, mainly ESR and CRP.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, here a sign of chronic inflammation.
glossary.BMI: Body mass index: weight in kg divided by height in metres squared.
glossary.visual symptoms: Problems with sight, such as blurring, double vision or loss of vision.
glossary.ultrasound: Imaging with sound waves, used here to look for bursitis and tenosynovitis.
glossary.steroid tapering: Slowly reducing the steroid dose over months to avoid relapse and adrenal crisis.
glossary.vitamin D: Vitamin needed to absorb calcium and keep bones strong.
glossary.calcium: The main mineral in bone, given with vitamin D for bone protection.
glossary.high-dose steroids: A large dose of prednisolone, or IV methylprednisolone if sight is threatened, given at once in GCA.
glossary.visual loss: Loss of sight, the feared complication of GCA.
glossary.medium/large arteries: Arteries such as the aorta, carotid and temporal arteries affected by GCA.
glossary.low-dose corticosteroids: Small steroid doses, such as prednisolone 15 mg daily, that control PMR.
glossary.ophthalmic artery: The artery supplying the eye and optic nerve.
glossary.temporal artery: The artery running over the temple at the side of the head, biopsied to diagnose GCA.
glossary.optic nerve: The nerve carrying signals from the eye to the brain.
glossary.irreversible: Cannot be undone; lost vision in GCA usually does not return.
glossary.bone resorption: Breakdown of bone by osteoclasts, releasing calcium into the blood.
glossary.fracture risk: The chance of breaking a bone, raised by osteoporosis and long-term steroids.
